1. (Currently amended) A catheter system for delivering ultrasonic energy to a treatment site within a body lumen, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal end, a distal end and an energy delivery section positioned between the proximal end and the distal end; a plurality of ultrasound radiating members positioned within the energy delivery section, the plurality of ultrasound radiating members being allocated into electrical groups comprising more than one ultrasound radiating member; wherein the ultrasound radiating members of one electrical group are spatially interdigitated with the ultrasound radiating members of another electrical group; and __wherein the ultrasound radiating members are configured to operate at different frequencies or phase angles to deliver therapeutic energy with enhanced penetration into tissue at the treatment site__.

2. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the plurality of ultrasound radiating members are mounted on an inner core, wherein the inner core is configured for insertion into the tubular body, __and wherein the inner core comprises a flexible substrate supporting the ultrasound radiating members in a non-uniform spatial distribution__.

3. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, further comprising at least one therapeutic compound delivery lumen that extends through the tubular body and terminates at least one outlet positioned in the energy delivery section, __wherein the at least one outlet is positioned between interdigitated ultrasound radiating members of different electrical groups__.

4. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a regular pattern, __and wherein the regular pattern comprises alternating members of first and second electrical groups with a spacing of less than one wavelength of the ultrasonic energy__.

5. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a pseudo random pattern, __wherein the pseudo random pattern is generated by a mathematical algorithm that ensures non-uniform distribution while maintaining electrical group separation__.

6. (Currently amended) A system for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the system comprising: a first and a second ultrasound catheters, each of the first and the second ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section having at least one ultrasound element, the tubular body also including at least one fluid delivery lumen; and a control system is connected to and configured to operate both the first and the second ultrasound catheters, __wherein the control system is configured to independently modulate the ultrasonic frequency or power output of each catheter__.

7. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 6, wherein the control system operates both the first and the second ultrasound catheters simultaneously, __and wherein the control system synchronizes the ultrasonic energy delivery between the first and second catheters with a phase offset__.

8. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 7, wherein the control system is configured to independently control the ultrasound radiating members on the first and the second ultrasound catheters, __such that ultrasound radiating members of different electrical groups on each catheter can be energized at different times or frequencies__.

9. (Currently amended) A method for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the method comprising: advancing an ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen; advancing the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter to a treatment site in the patient's pulmonary artery; inflating a balloon on the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter; delivering a thrombolytic drug to the treatment site through the at least one fluid delivery lumen; and emitting ultrasonic energy to thereby promote diffusion of the thrombolytic drug at the treatment site, __wherein the ultrasonic energy is emitted at a frequency greater than 1 MHz and with a duty cycle of less than 50%__.

10. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 9, wherein delivering the thrombolytic drug and emitting ultrasonic energy are performed simultaneously, __and wherein the ultrasonic energy is modulated to create acoustic cavitation at the treatment site__.

11. (Currently amended) An ultrasound catheter for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen, the tubular body defining a guidewire lumen extending through the proximal portion and the ultrasound energy delivery section, __wherein the at least one ultrasound element comprises a plurality of interdigitated radiating members allocated into at least two electrical groups__.

12. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, wherein the guidewire lumen extends through the at least one ultrasound element, __and wherein the guidewire lumen is positioned centrally through the ultrasound energy delivery section__.

13. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, further comprising at least one balloon positioned at the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter, __wherein the at least one balloon is configured to maintain the distal portion in contact with vessel wall tissue during ultrasonic energy delivery__.
